feat(doctor): align doctor, an install preflight that makes a real tools/call (ALI-1740) (#431)

`align doctor` prints PASS, FAIL or SKIP for Node (>=22.16), `align` on PATH
(the spawnable form on Windows), gateway reachable, whoami, and one real
`tools/call` of align_ask through `align mcp`. It exits non-zero on any
failure, an empty answer is a failure, and each failure names the next step.

It sends no telemetry of any kind, in the process or in the `align mcp` it
starts: the run is exempt from the notice, the install beacon and the usage
ping, and the child carries ALIGN_DOCTOR=1, which the one telemetry gate
reads. It is not DO_NOT_TRACK on purpose: an env opt-out is stored as a
permanent opt-out in the user's config.

scripts/smoke-mcp-handshake.mjs gains the same tools/call step (and an
optional env argument), so CI cannot go green on tools/list alone, which is
answered locally and passes with a wrong-type credential.

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(context): a local graph's decisions file stays out of git (#418)

* fix(context): a local graph's decisions file stays out of git

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(context): a local graph's decisions file lives in ~/.align, not just gitignored (ALI-1652)

gitignore is a convention anyone can bypass - edit the line, `git add -f`,
a merge that drops it - and this file's whole stated purpose is to carry
content from a personal local graph that must not leave the machine
without `align share`'s controls (preview, secret scan, consent). Every
other piece of local-only state this CLI keeps (saved tokens, the local
graph DB itself) already lives under ~/.align for exactly this reason;
this file was the one exception.

writeDecisionsContext now takes an `external` option. For a local graph,
the real bytes go to ~/.align/contexts/<hash-of-repo-path>/decisions.md
(0600, same as every other file under ~/.align) and a SYMLINK is left at
.align/decisions.md pointing there - so the CLAUDE.md import, `align
context inject`, and the existing gitignore/tracked-by-git checks all
keep working completely unchanged, because a normal file read follows a
symlink transparently. A team graph's file is unaffected: still a real,
shareable, committable file, since that content is meant to be shared.

Symlinks need POSIX semantics Windows does not give an unprivileged
process, so on win32 this falls back to the plain in-repo file (today's
behaviour) - best effort, same shape as the platform-dependent hardening
already in private-files.ts.

Verified the new tests actually catch a regression: disabled the
symlinkSync call, watched 7 tests fail, restored, confirmed green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: force single-threaded vitest on win32 to stop RPC-heartbeat timeouts (ALI-1669)

Manually dispatched cross-platform (windows-latest) on this branch to
prove the earlier fixes: 7039/7039 tests passed, zero failures. The job
still exited 1, from 2 "Unhandled Error" entries unrelated to any test:

  Error: [vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"

This is vitest's own internal worker<->main-process RPC heartbeat,
not a test. Under 2 worker threads contending for the runner's 2
cores, the round-trip apparently misses its internal timeout (not
configurable directly - it's inside vitest/birpc) under load, and
vitest treats that as a hard, run-failing error even though every
actual test passed. This did not appear on either of the two prior
Windows runs I checked, consistent with it being a contention
symptom rather than a deterministic bug - but unlike the test-level
timeouts, this one fails the WHOLE run regardless of test results,
so it is worth removing the contention rather than accepting it.

poolOptions.threads.singleThread removes the only lever that changes
without touching a single test: all files run in one thread instead
of two parallel workers, so there is nothing left to contend with the
RPC heartbeat for the main thread's attention. Scoped to win32 only;
costs roughly 2x wall-clock there, which is acceptable since this
config only applies on a job that already never runs on a normal PR
(push-to-main or a manual proof-before-merge dispatch only).

* fix: widen rmDir's retry budget - 5.5s was not enough under contention (ALI-1669)

Third manual Windows verification run: zero RPC timeouts (the 32-file
timeout fix resolved that), zero timed-out tests, but one new,
different, genuine failure:

  Error: EBUSY: resource busy or locked, rmdir
    '...align-l6-launcher-e2e-PJFvyw\home'

launcher-child-telemetry-e2e.test.ts already does the right thing
before calling rmDir: it waits for the tracked child PID to actually
exit (waitPidGone), SIGKILLs if it will not, waits again, then only
then removes the directory. It still hit EBUSY, because fs.rmSync's
own retry budget here (maxRetries: 10, retryDelay: 100) is linear
backoff, not flat delay - total wait is retryDelay * N * (N+1) / 2, so
the real budget was ~5.5s, not the ~1s it reads as. Under the same
contention this whole PR has been fighting, a lingering OS-level file
handle (the process's own exit vs the OS actually releasing the
handle is not instantaneous, and can lag further under load) didn't
clear inside that window.

Shared helper (13 call sites), so this benefits every e2e test that
spawns a real child process, not just this one. (20, 150) is ~31.5s.
These options are a documented no-op on POSIX (the error codes they
retry on - EBUSY/EPERM from rmdir - are a Windows-only failure mode),
so this costs nothing anywhere else.

Full suite still green: 456/456 files, 7166/7174 tests.

* feat(local): harden the local graph at rest - owner-only files, write-time secret redaction, backup exclusion

No full SQLite encryption (a key would sit next to the file); tighten around it instead.

Permissions (macOS/Linux; Windows relies on the profile ACL, documented):
- New private-files.ts: directories 0700 and files 0600 on create whatever the umask, and any
  group/world bit removed on every open.
- The graph: createLocalDb pre-creates local.db 0600 before SQLite opens it (SQLite's default is
  0644; the -wal/-shm take the main file's mode) and tightens the dir and all three files on open.
  Every short-lived opener (ledger, judgements, guardrail, sync state, classify, scope defaults,
  source sync) re-checks too.
- config.json and its directory are tightened when the store opens; both one-time directory
  migrations copy into a private place. Pending-share/request dirs, the advisory verdict store,
  the advisory dedup marker, blocked-source markers and the embedding model cache likewise.

Secrets: the vendored share scanner gains redactSecrets, which replaces each match with the
pattern's placeholder (keeping a captured prefix, as brain does). ingestOne runs it on the text,
title override and source URL before anything reads them, so capture, every import, sessions and
MCP align_capture never store a raw secret; mark notes are redacted in upsertJudgement. One notice
per run (cli.ts postAction, index.ts exit fallback); align_capture returns secretsRedacted and the
mark outcome says it. Fast on 200 KB inputs.

Backups: on macOS the graph dir gets a sticky Time Machine exclusion (tmutil, only if present) and
every OS gets CACHEDIR.TAG, once, best effort, never fatal; wired into initLocalMode and startup.

Docs: "What Align stores on your machine and how it is protected" in docs/local-mode.md, and a
data-at-rest section in SECURITY.md.

Test harness: the simulated-macOS share tests set ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH, because the faked platform
made esbuild throw on any cold tsx cache (all four failed on a cold cache, before this change too).
